svg.text: Single host: Windows laptop · Docker Desktop (WSL2) · 16 GB RAM · every server container limited to 1 CPU
A, B (and C) of a block share one seed; arm order randomised with a logged seed
docker compose · docker kill · Docker stats API
same code and seeds for every arm · excluded from resource measurement

g.text: Synthetic exam (5 MB, seeded) → AES-256-GCM encryption
Exam key → Shamir k-of-n split (k = 3, n = 5)
Registration with the arm; T0 on a whole second, ~15 s later
(Arm C stores the key itself; no trustees)
Each submits its share at T0 (retries while "too early")
Arm B: share signed with the trustee's Ed25519 key
Sensitivity / faults: jitter 0–30 s, absent, corrupted,
Verify each share against its commitment (B: and signature)
Rebuild the key from k shares, check its SHA-256
Arrival time after T0 per centre → L50, L95, Lmax
Early key (before T0) counted as a safety failure
Oracle: decrypt the exam once, compare its SHA-256
Sensitivity: M = 10 / 200, polling 200 / 1000 ms, exam 1 / 20 MB

svg.text: Arm A · threshold + smart contract (Hyperledger Besu, QBFT)

g.text: QBFT consensus · block period 2 s (sensitivity 1 s / 5 s) · tolerates 1 faulty validator
Every validator holds the contract state (replicated ledger)
Trustee i sends its transaction to validator (i mod 4) + 1
Centres read from their own validator, fail over to the others

svg.text: Arm B · threshold + replicated coordinator (etcd, Raft)

g.text: Accepts a share only after T0,
Share record = keys in etcd (one operator)

svg.text: Arm C · central key server (reference only)
Key server (1 CPU): returns the key after T0
one operator, one clock, no threshold

server containers only → CPU-seconds, peak memory
